title: Kitchen Orientation & Tools
subtitle: A tool is a job. And why a sharp knife is the safe one.
objectives: Name the main kitchen tools and their jobs
Choose the right tool for a task
Explain why a sharp knife is safer than a dull one
Handle knives and hot tools safely

cards.title: A tool is a job, not an object
cards.text: A drawer full of named things is not a skill. Knowing which one the job needs (and why that one) is.

cards.title: Six tools cover almost everything
cards.text: Start here and you can cook most things.
points: **Chef's knife**: most cutting.
**Paring knife**: small work held in your hand.
**Measuring cups and spoons**: "a bit" is not a quantity.
**Colander, tongs, thermometer**: separate, move, check.

cards.title: Six tools, and the job each one is for
cards.text: Tap each tool. The second line is why that one and not another.

question.text: Which tool tells you whether chicken is actually safe?
question.explain: 74°C inside, measured. Colour is not doneness.

cards.title: A sharp knife is the safe one
cards.text: This sounds wrong and is not.
points: **A dull blade slides** instead of biting.
**So you push harder.**
**When it finally slips** it slips with all that force.
**A sharp knife needs almost none.**

question.text: A dull knife is more dangerous because…
options: you have to push harder, so a slip carries more force
question.explain: Force plus a slip is the whole problem.

cards.title: Four habits, not four rules
cards.text: Rules are forgotten. Habits run without you.
points: **The claw:** fingertips curled under, knuckles guide the blade.
**Cut on a board that does not move.** Damp cloth underneath.
**Carry a knife point down**, blade behind you.
**Never put a knife in the washing-up water.**

cards.title: A rice cooker has no timer in it
cards.text: It is a magnet that gives up at the right moment, and that is the whole design.
points: **While there is water**, the pot stays at 100°C.
**Water gone, the pot climbs** past that.
**A ferrite magnet loses its grip** at about 103°C.
**The switch drops to warm.** No clock, no sensor, no chip.

cards.title: Wrapping hands is mise en place
cards.text: Nobody wraps their hands halfway through a round.
points: **Everything ready before the bell.**
**Gloves, wraps, water, mouthguard.**
**Same in a kitchen:** everything out before any heat.
**Heat starts a clock** you cannot pause.

question.text: Where should a knife never be put?
question.explain: Somebody reaches into the water and finds it with a hand.

cards.title: Six tools, most of a kitchen
cards.alt: A chef's knife, a paring knife, measuring cups and spoons, a colander, tongs and a probe thermometer
cards.text: Name the job of each one. The thermometer is the only one that tells you something is safe.

cards.title: A recipe is a torque spec
cards.text: Numbers in both exist because guessing damages the thing.
points: **"Tighten it well" strips a thread.**
**"Add a bit of salt" ruins a dish.**
**Both have a right value** somebody measured.
**Measuring spoons are not fussiness.** They are the spec.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Chef's knife for most cutting; paring knife for hand work.
A thermometer, not colour, tells you food is safe.
Sharp knives are safer. Less force, less slip.
Everything out and prepped before any heat.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 1 TLE. Tools are introduced by the job they do rather than as a labelled drawer, and the week's argument is that six tools cover almost everything, which is more useful than naming twenty. The counter-intuitive safety fact (a sharp knife is safer because it needs less force) gets its own card and a checkpoint, because it is the one that changes behaviour. The rice cooker teardown is the strongest hook in the week and is accurate: a Curie-point ferrite magnet releases the switch once the water is gone and the pot climbs past 100°C. The car lens defends measuring spoons on the only ground he will accept: they are a spec.
discussion: Ask which tool he would reach for, and why that one.
Ask why a dull knife is the dangerous one.
Ask what a rice cooker uses instead of a timer.
Ask what mise en place means in boxing terms.
extension: Have him set up a workstation for one dish before cooking anything.
Have him open a rice cooker base and find the thermostat.
misconceptions: "Dull knives are safer." They need more force, so slips cost more.
"Colour tells you chicken is done." A thermometer does.
"Measuring is fussy." Baking is a ratio.
